summary: Fitzhugh Sound light on Addenbroke Island: lit 1914 from a dwelling with a lantern room; the round concrete tower dates from 1998; staffed, reached by boat.

structures.type: two-storey dwelling with octagonal lantern room
steel skeletal tower on the dwelling

staffing.basis: Lighthouse Friends keeper list to 2024 (Tim Rogers, 2023 to at least 2024); Rowlett describes a staffed light station; the Coast Guard's 2024 release does not name Addenbroke among the two stations where keeper functions ended.

events.note: Work begun by day labour under D. McLean (Lighthouse Friends)

corrections.why: The record's 9.0 m is an OpenStreetMap-derived figure; Rowlett's Lighthouse Directory gives 8 m (26 ft) for the round concrete tower built in 1998.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record conflicts 1914 (Rowlett's station established; Marine report fiscal 1913-14; Lighthouse Friends first lighting 15 April 1914) against 1998 (the current round tower). The story dates the station to 1914 and the present tower to 1998.
OSM's 9 m for the tower differs from Rowlett's 8 m (26 ft) for the same round concrete tower; the story gives no tower height, and the correction is proposed above for the editor.
Lighthouse Friends says he had served two years at Lucy Island; the 1928 Colonist says he had been keeper there 'for a long time'. The story gives both.

Lighthouse Friends names a man (Calvert Thorpe) who found the body on the morning of 16 August; the 1928 Colonist dispatch says a fisherman reported it. The story says 'Lighthouse Friends says' and the Colonist's version separately, and names neither man.
The 2010 CCG table in the Senate report marks Addenbroke as automated (aids can work without a keeper) while listing two permanent residents. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: (1) Marine 1914 table (scan 57, printed p. 50): the BC changes list names Addenbrooke, Aiskin Island, Greene Point and Langara, and the work lines are separate OCR columns. The line 'Erection of a combined light-house and dwelling' is matched to Addenbrooke by its position as the first station; check the page image before citing the row to a station. (2) Daily Colonist: the OCR masthead reads 'SATURDAY, AUGUST 16, 1928'; the issue is dated 18 August by its place in the run (the dispatch is datelined 17 August). Confirm the masthead on the page image. (3) Finder conflict: Lighthouse Friends names a man who found the body on the morning of 16 August; the 1928 Colonist says a fisherman reported it. The story says 'Lighthouse Friends says' for the morning and does not name either man. (4) Lighthouse Friends names a police corporal and a drifter suspected in the death; neither is named in the story, and the sources read do not record the outcome of the inquiry. (5) The keeper list is Lighthouse Friends' only. The 1916 Marine statement of BC keepers puts 'W. G. Guthro' near a different station in the OCR, so Guthro is not confirmed in a primary source for this station. (6) The Senate table's other columns are unlabelled in our OCR; only 'Permanent residents' is quoted. (7) Staffing today: Lighthouse Friends lists a keeper for 2023 to at least 2024 and Rowlett describes a staffed station; the 2024 Coast Guard release does not name Addenbroke. The record's 'check' flag stands. (8) Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett are copyrighted; the story paraphrases them with one short quotation from each. (9) The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights page for Queen Charlotte Sound was cached only in part and does not show the Addenbroke entry; not cited. (10) No photos added. (11) The 1913 start and the 1914 lighting rest on Lighthouse Friends and the Marine report; the report's entry shows the works, not the first lighting date. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28 (independent checker): (a) Quote check passed on first run (0 missing). (b) Marine report scan 57 / printed 50 confirmed by corpus.py page (no '?'); the Addenbrooke row is matched to the first work item by OCR position and is corroborated by Lighthouse Friends' 'day labour under D. McLean'; the page image could not be fetched (IIIF host returned 502), so this stays a position match. (c) Colonist masthead on the page with the Maynard item is garbled but reads Saturday August 18, 1928 (18 Aug 1928 was a Saturday), so the footnote date stands. (d) The 2010 Senate table (Appendix 4) marks Addenbroke 'Yes' in the automated column; the report's text says nine of 27 Pacific staffed stations are automated, and the count of 'Yes' entries in that column is nine. (e) The 2024 CCG release does not name Addenbroke; it states the twenty-five other staffed BC light stations will continue normally. (f) Rowlett's 'Staffed light station' description is undated on the page (2025 photo credits). (g) The Maynard shooting is described from two sources; the story names no suspect and no finder, per the living/private-person rule, and gives no outcome because none is in the sources.
